scenes.title: Wilderness · Old Owl Well · undead revealed
Cragmaw Castle · Cragmaw Castle · king's quarters

encounters.name: Old Owl Well · optional fight
encounters.note: Hamun Kost and up to twelve zombies. Parley is the intended first contact; reveal undead when they emerge.

encounters.name: Wyvern Tor · optional camp
encounters.note: One sentry, six ordinary orcs inside, Brughor (30 HP), and Gog the ogre. Extremely dangerous for low-level PCs.

encounters.name: Thundertree 1 · Western cottage
encounters.note: Two hidden twig blights; area 2 may attract them.

encounters.name: Thundertree 2 · Blighted cottages
encounters.note: Six twig blights; move surviving area-1 blights if they join.

encounters.name: Thundertree 3 · Brown Horse
encounters.note: Four ash zombies; track each first-damage Ash Puff.

encounters.name: Thundertree 5 · Farmhouse
encounters.note: Eight twig blights may approach doorways in pairs.

encounters.name: Thundertree 6 · Spider store
encounters.note: Two hidden giant spiders and restraining webs.

encounters.name: Thundertree 7 · Venomfang
encounters.note: Young green dragon; very dangerous for level-2 party. Parley and retreat are supported.

encounters.name: Thundertree 8 · Smithy
encounters.note: Two ash zombies; first-damage Ash Puff.

encounters.name: Thundertree 11 · Garrison
encounters.note: Five ash zombies; old armor does not improve AC.

encounters.name: Thundertree 12 · Weaver’s cottage
encounters.note: Six twig blights; noise alerts area 13.

encounters.name: Thundertree 13 · Dragon cultists
encounters.note: Six cultists including Favric; they prefer talking.

encounters.name: Castle 3 · Arrow-slit posts
encounters.note: Two goblins in each post. They warn areas 4 and 6 if they spot an intruder.

encounters.name: Castle 2 · Falling rubble
encounters.note: Passive Perception 20 or active DC 10 Perception while searching; DC 10 Dexterity save, 3d6 bludgeoning or half.

encounters.name: Castle 4 · Ruined barracks
encounters.note: Three goblins; loud noise attracts a scout from the banquet hall.

encounters.name: Castle 6 · Hobgoblin barracks
encounters.note: Four hobgoblins, AC 18; remember Martial Advantage.

encounters.name: Castle 7 · Banquet hall
encounters.note: Yegg (12 HP) plus seven goblins; account for any scout who left.

encounters.name: Castle 8 · Dark hall
encounters.note: One grick on an upper ledge. Check sight and surprise, then reveal it.

encounters.name: Castle 9 · Goblin shrine
encounters.note: Lhupo (12 HP) and two goblins. They prepare if the grick fight was heard.

encounters.name: Castle 12 · Guard barracks
encounters.note: Two hobgoblins; one warns Grol and returns two rounds later.

encounters.name: Castle 13 · Owlbear tower
encounters.note: One owlbear. Fresh meat or an opened exit can avoid combat.

encounters.name: Castle 14 · King’s quarters
encounters.note: Grol (45 HP), Snarl (18 HP), Vyerith disguised as a drow, and Gundren stable at 0 HP.

encounters.name: Optional · Returning war band
encounters.note: Targor (20 HP), two hobgoblins, and two wolves; negotiation is possible.

runbookBeats.title: Before play · carry forward what actually happened
ask: Where did Session 2 end? Did anyone identify the Redbrands as Gundren’s abductors or learn Cragmaw Castle’s location?
Were the wagon and Lionshield goods delivered? Which rewards were actually paid?
Is Iarno captured, escaped, or still in his quarters? Are Mirna, Nars, Nilsa, and Droop safe?
What are the five current levels, HP, spell slots, supplies, and Sildar’s equipment?
run: If play stopped mid-hideout or mid-combat, continue the existing Session 2 save. Make this new pack only after that scene resolves.
Session 1 remains fixed: Klarg died, Yeemik kept the hideout, Sildar was rescued, and Trista privately took the BELOW token. Donavan noticed concealment, not the object.
DM truth: Redbrands took Gundren to Cragmaw Castle. Players learn this only if a witness or evidence established it during play.
Do not assume the party reached level 3. The castle is dangerous to a depleted level-2 party; make scouting, retreat, and negotiation meaningful.
runbookBeats.tv: Keep the town map or a neutral title on the TV while you reconcile the last session.
private: Sources: Lost Mine of Phandelver pp. 27 and 35–41; Session 1 actual recap and the recorded Session 2 outcome.

runbookBeats.title: 1 · Choose the lead, not the destination
read: Morning trade returns to Phandalin, but every familiar doorway now seems to hold a different answer. Somewhere beyond town, Gundren is still missing. Which lead do you follow first?
ask: What evidence do you trust? Who comes with you? What do you buy, borrow, or leave behind?
run: If Iarno’s transfer record was found, it names Cragmaw Castle as the destination. A captured Redbrand can establish the gang’s role without necessarily knowing the route.
Qelline can suggest Reidoth near Thundertree; Halia knows the gang has a goblin with a castle lead; a captured bugbear can give a more precise lead. Agatha can answer one carefully chosen question.
If no castle lead was earned, offer a real inquiry, tracks, or an NPC the party already trusts. Never narrate the hidden destination as common knowledge.
choices: Castle known: let the party plan travel and scouting.
Castle unknown: play the chosen lead below.
Another quest chosen: use the linked location scene and return to this decision when they have new evidence.
runbookBeats.tv: Show the player-safe Phandalin map. Publish only leads the characters heard.
private: The transfer record is an Echo Below campaign addition, not printed treasure. Source: adventure pp. 14–18, 27–29.

runbookBeats.title: 2 · Triboar Trail and Neverwinter Wood
read: The last chimney smoke falls behind you. The trail runs between long grasses and dark stands of trees, then narrows until every snapped twig sounds close.
ask: What is the marching order, travel pace, light plan, and watch schedule? Is anyone tracking a specific sign?
run: The adventure uses roughly 24 miles in a ten-hour travel day, with eight hours of rest. Mark actual time and supplies rather than teleporting between sites.

If using the published wandering table, check once by day and once by night: d20 result 17–20 brings a random encounter. Roll its creature only after the check succeeds; do not deploy all possible groups.
A captured goblin or hobgoblin can provide castle directions according to the adventure. Let the party use stealth, avoidance, parley, or retreat.
choices: If the group heads to a town lead, jump to that scene.
If the castle route is known, move to the approach beat.
runbookBeats.tv: Show trail art; switch to the woodland or night-camp battle map only if a specific encounter occurs.
private: Adventure pp. 27–28. Do not reveal a castle marker on the TV map before the party knows its location.

runbookBeats.title: Optional lead · Conyberry and Agatha
read: Beyond the ruined village, branches bend together into a low shelter. The air stills. A voice from within sounds older than the trees: “You came this far to ask me something?”
ask: What single question matters most, and who speaks for the group? Do you offer Sister Garaele’s comb?
run: Agatha is a social encounter. Respectful conversation and DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) can win one answer; the silver comb from Sister Garaele secures her cooperation. A player who roleplays the exchange well has advantage.
She answers one question. She can address the castle’s location if asked, but the party may instead ask about Bowgentle’s book or something else. Record the precise answer.
If insulted or threatened, she withdraws rather than starting a mandatory fight. The prepared reward is 200 XP for successfully obtaining an answer if using XP.
choices: If Agatha provides the route, go to the castle approach.
If she answers a different question, follow that consequence.
runbookBeats.tv: Show Conyberry ruins, then the woven shelter. Reveal Agatha’s portrait only when she appears.
private: Adventure pp. 28–29. Agatha’s information is not a general reveal of the Echo mystery.

runbookBeats.title: Optional lead · Old Owl Well
read: A broken watchtower rises above a quiet courtyard. A tidy tent sits beside a working well. The ruins smell of dust, old stone, and something less wholesome beneath them.
ask: Do you approach openly, call out, or investigate the ruins first? What do you ask Hamun Kost?
run: Twelve zombies are concealed in the tower until the party approaches the tent or tower. Hamun Kost can call them off temporarily while speaking.
Kost is willing to trade information for a favor: remove the Wyvern Tor orcs or ask Agatha who built the tower. He is not an automatic combat encounter.
If the party reports a parley to Daran, track that quest. If violence starts, use the printed room and monster cards; twelve zombies plus a mage are a serious threat.
choices: A bargain can redirect the party to Agatha or Wyvern Tor.
The party can withdraw without completing Daran’s errand.
runbookBeats.tv: Show the ruined well. Do not show the undead reveal until the zombies emerge.
private: Adventure p. 29. Keep Kost’s tent treasure private until found; do not put twelve hidden zombies on the TV.

runbookBeats.title: If violence starts · Old Owl Well
ask: Where are the PCs relative to the tower, well, and tent? Did Kost call a halt before spells were cast?
run: Twelve zombies can emerge from the tower. Hamun Kost uses the Evil Mage base spells without Iarno’s staff; AC 12, HP 22, spell save DC 13, +5 spell attacks. Keep any survivors and negotiations from the preceding conversation.
Zombie: AC 8, HP 22, slam +3 for 1d6+1. At 0 HP, Undead Fortitude may leave it at 1 HP unless radiant damage or a critical hit caused the drop.
Do not deploy every zombie at once unless they are actually visible and participating. This whole camp is a severe fight for low-level PCs; give routes to retreat.
runbookBeats.tv: Switch to the well battle map only when position matters. Reveal zombies as they emerge, not at scene start.
private: Adventure p. 29; Evil Mage p. 57; SRD 5.1 Zombie pp. 356–357.

runbookBeats.title: Optional lead · Wyvern Tor
read: Smoke threads up from a notch in the stony ridge. Below it, a narrow ravine bends toward a cave mouth. A lone watcher stands outside, far enough away to call a warning.
ask: Do you watch, negotiate, bypass the camp, or try to silence the sentry? Where is everyone?
run: Finding the hidden camp calls for DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) or DC 10 Wisdom (Survival) per hour by the lead character.
Inside are Brughor Axe-Biter, six ordinary orcs, and Gog the ogre; one additional orc watches outside. The sentry runs to warn them if it spots the party and survives.
This group is extremely dangerous for five level-2 characters. Show numbers and an exit; stealth, withdrawal, negotiation, and completing another lead first are valid.
The cave chest contains 750 cp, 180 sp, 62 ep, 30 gp, and three perfume vials worth 10 gp each; award only if found and taken.
choices: If the party leaves, the orcs remain a Phandalin threat.
If they win or strike a deal, return to Harbin or Kost as appropriate.
runbookBeats.tv: Use the ravine battle map only when the camp is located; place the sentry before the cave group.
private: Adventure p. 35. Count one outside sentry, six ordinary orcs inside, Brughor at 30 HP, and Gog the ogre. Do not accidentally omit the sentry.

runbookBeats.title: If the camp fights · Wyvern Tor
ask: Was the sentry silenced? Which defenders heard a warning, and what cover does each side have?
run: Sentry: one ordinary orc outside. Inside: six ordinary orcs, Brughor at 30 HP, and Gog the ogre. Use waves to avoid silently placing unseen enemies.
Orc: AC 13, HP 15, greataxe +5 for 1d12+3, javelin +5 for 1d6+3, and Aggressive bonus-action movement toward a visible hostile creature.
Ogre: AC 11, HP 59, greatclub +6 for 2d8+4 or javelin +6 for 2d6+4. After Brughor falls, surviving orcs flee according to the adventure.
This is a major threat. Do not add wandering enemies on top of it without an actual cause.
runbookBeats.tv: Show the ravine battle map. Start with the sentry, then reveal the cave force if it arrives.
private: Adventure p. 35; 2014 SRD 5.1 Orc p. 339 and Ogre p. 336.

runbookBeats.title: Optional lead · Reidoth at Thundertree
read: A weathered warning faces the road into an overgrown village. Roofs are broken, walls lean into vines, and the hilltop tower still stands above them all.
ask: Are you seeking Reidoth, scouting ruins, or following another reason to enter?
run: Reidoth can identify the castle’s location, but the village is a separate, larger adventure site. Do not imply the party must clear it to earn his help.

If the players explore buildings, continue to the Thundertree area beats in this runbook. All thirteen areas, local maps, optional fights, and Reidoth’s information are prepared; reveal only locations reached in play.
Warn in-world about plant monsters, undead, and the dragon; do not reveal those tokens or portraits before the characters encounter them.
runbookBeats.tv: Use the unmarked town map with fog; keep dragon, cultists, and building contents hidden.
private: Adventure pp. 30–35. This beat opens the optional village route; the area beats follow before the castle approach.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 1 · Western cottage
read: A roofless cottage crouches beneath a broad tree. Its doorway has almost vanished into weeds.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: Two twig blights hide beside the entrance. Compare their Stealth to passive Perception; if fighting breaks out, they can aid area 2.
Twig blight: AC 13, HP 4, claws +3 for 1d4+1 piercing; vulnerable to fire.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 2 · Blighted cottages
read: Two collapsed homes stand side by side, their old rooms given over to brush and young trees.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: Six twig blights wait in the growth; the two from area 1 join after one round if still alive and nearby.
A careful search and DC 10 Perception finds a chest with 700 cp, 160 sp, and 90 gp.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 3 · The Brown Horse
read: A faded horse sign hangs above the door of an old tavern. Inside, forms slump against the walls and beneath the bar.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: Four ash zombies rise when living creatures enter. They start prone; standing uses half their speed.

Ash Puff: the first time each zombie takes damage, creatures within 5 feet make DC 10 Constitution saves or suffer disadvantage on attacks, saves, and checks for one minute; repeat the save at turn end. Track each zombie separately.
Zombie: AC 8, HP 22, slam +3 for 1d6+1; check Undead Fortitude at 0 HP.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 4 · Reidoth’s watch
read: One cottage seems to have resisted the years. Its shutters are stout, and someone has cleared the growth near the door.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: Reidoth is direct but reasonably hospitable. He tells the party how to reach Cragmaw Castle if asked; no dragon bargain is required for those directions.

He warns of ash zombies, plant creatures, spiders, cultists, and a young green dragon. He knows where Wave Echo Cave is but offers that location only if the party drives the dragon off; he will not accompany them inside.
If attacked, he uses his druid shape to flee and waits for the aggressors to leave. Record whether the party earns his trust.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 5 · Blighted farmhouse
read: The farmhouse walls have collapsed into a knot of gorse. Something small shifts in the leaves when you disturb the stones.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: Eight twig blights lurk in the thicket. If disturbed, two head for each of two doorways every round for three rounds. This is not one instant visible swarm.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 6 · Ruined store and webs
read: White strands cross the lane to a broken store. The building looks empty from outside, though its walls offer plenty of shadows.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: Two giant spiders hide inside. Webbed squares are difficult terrain; DC 10 Athletics crosses, failure restrains. A restrained creature may use an action for DC 12 Strength; a light slashing weapon can cut a web (AC 10, HP 5, vulnerable to fire).
Spider: AC 14, HP 26; bite +5 for 1d8+3 piercing plus DC 11 Constitution save against 2d8 poison (half on success); web +5 can restrain and recharges on 5–6.
A cocooned adventurer holds a healing potion, 23 gp, and 35 sp.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 7 · Venomfang’s tower
read: A broken tower rises above two spider corpses. The air around it smells sharp and wrong; the upper roof is open to the sky.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: Venomfang is a young green dragon: AC 18, HP 136, fly 60, poison breath DC 16 Constitution for 12d6 poison in a 30-foot cone, half on success. It is far beyond a routine level-2 fight.
Give players visible signs of danger and time to retreat or parley. Venomfang values its lair; if reduced to half HP it flies away. It may hear loud cottage activity and ambush.

Tower chest: 800 sp, 150 gp, four 60-gp silver goblets, misty step and lightning bolt scrolls. Hew, a +1 battleaxe with extra damage against plants and wood objects, lies under the coin. Reveal only when found.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 8 · Old smithy
read: Rotten wood and a wide chimney mark the old forge. Two ash-covered shapes slump where the anvils once stood.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: Two ash zombies rise when the party enters and pursue after they see a target. Use the same Ash Puff timing and saves as area 3.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 9 · Herbalist’s shop
read: Broken bottles and unreadable books fill an old shop. Mirna’s description points you toward the storage shelves.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: If Mirna Dendrar sent them, the heirloom case is found automatically. Otherwise DC 15 Perception finds it behind the shelves.
Inside is her emerald necklace worth 200 gp. Record whether the party returns it; doing so earns the printed reward if using XP.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 10 · Town square
read: A leaning warrior statue watches over a square almost swallowed by brush. Paths leave in several directions.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: DC 15 History identifies the old hero as Palien. DC 20 Strength can topple the statue if someone tries.
Let the party choose the next building by what they see on the player map; do not push them toward the dragon.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 11 · Old garrison
read: An old stone barracks still has a roof and narrow windows. Rusted armor lies among the beds.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: Five ash zombies wake when disturbed. Their scraps of armor do not improve AC 8. Use Ash Puff and Undead Fortitude as in area 3.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 12 · Weaver’s cottage
read: A broken loom sits in a cottage open to the weather. Thick growth hides the ground beyond its southern wall.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: Six twig blights wait in the southern thicket. Compare Stealth to Perception before initiative.
Loud combat here draws cautious investigation by the cultists in area 13.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: Thundertree 13 · Dragon cultists
read: The shutters of this apparently empty house are barred from within. You hear low voices behind them.
ask: How do you approach, and where is each character?
run: Six cultists live here. Their leader Favric wants to make an alliance with the dragon; the others prefer to survive. They are willing to talk and need not fight.
If the party seems interested in the dragon, Favric may offer to introduce them as a tribute. Do not hide his intention if the players probe his story.
Cultist: AC 12, HP 9, scimitar +3 for 1d6+1. Favric has the same combat block. Favric carries a potion of flying; a coffer holds three diamonds worth 100 gp each.
The door is barred from within (DC 20 Strength); shutters DC 15 Strength.
runbookBeats.tv: Show only this location and creatures the characters have discovered. Keep other buildings fogged.
private: Lost Mine of Phandelver (2014), printed pp. 30–35; use its private marked map for exact building positions.

runbookBeats.title: 3 · Cragmaw Castle comes into view
read: The trees give way to a low rise. Seven broken towers crowd around a ruined stronghold. The place looks abandoned until you catch a small movement behind a narrow slit in the stone.
ask: How long do you watch? Do you seek another entry, wear a disguise, or approach the gate?
run: The main gate is ruined. Arrow slits give three-quarters cover to defenders firing through them. Interior doors are reinforced but unlocked; DC 15 Strength forces one.
The book explicitly supports bluffing with Redbrand cloaks and a claim to be Glasstaff’s envoys. Resolve a group deception against defenders’ Insight; do not decide the route for the party.
At night the interior is dark. During day only limited light enters through arrow slits. Ask for torches and darkvision.
choices: A concealed north entrance can be discovered near area 11.
runbookBeats.tv: Show the castle approach illustration. Stage the unmarked castle map privately; keep fog fully closed.
private: Adventure pp. 35–37. The marked map at p. 37 is DM-only. The TV map is an unmarked interpretation.

runbookBeats.title: 4 · Begin castle exploration
ask: Which entrance do you use? Who is first? What light is visible to the defenders?
run: Keep an alarm note: quiet, suspicious, or raised. Once raised, nearby room groups can respond according to their keyed descriptions.
The party can retreat through any route it actually opened. Resting inside a guarded castle has consequences; make the situation clear before a rest.
Use the printed room map for distances and door placement. The TV map is a player-safe tactical interpretation.
runbookBeats.tv: Show the unmarked castle map with fog. Reveal one entered space at a time. Do not deploy the entire garrison.
private: Adventure map p. 37; keyed rooms pp. 36–41.

runbookBeats.title: Area 1 · Entrance and sentries
read: Shattered gate timbers lie across an old entrance. Above the wreckage, narrow slots stare out from two small chambers.
ask: Do you move quietly, call out, or look for another way in?
run: There are two goblins in each area-3 archer post, four total. They glance out only intermittently. Compare the party’s Stealth to their passive Perception rather than granting automatic detection.
If they see intruders, they shoot from behind arrow-slit cover and shout. They cannot fire directly at enemies who have passed the broken gate.
Their alarm can bring goblins from area 4 and hobgoblins from area 6 into area 2.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal the gate and two arrow-slit posts. Keep the goblins hidden until noticed or until they fire.
private: Adventure p. 36. Each pair is a separate 100-XP group if using XP.

runbookBeats.title: Area 2 · Falling rubble
read: A wide hall disappears into half-light. Dust lies thick around a pile of fallen plaster, and closed doors lead away on either side.
ask: Where does each character step? Is anyone actively searching the damaged ceiling or floor?
run: The hidden tripwire is spotted by passive Perception 20 or active DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) while searching this area. Once found, it is easy to avoid or disable without a check.
A creature that crosses the rubble without avoiding it triggers a ceiling collapse. Creatures in the marked area make DC 10 Dexterity saves: 3d6 bludgeoning on failure, half on success.
The noise alerts areas 3, 7, 8, and 9. Record the alarm before moving to another room.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal the hall. Show the collapse only after it is detected or triggered.
private: Adventure p. 36. The TV map must not pre-mark the tripwire or exact fall zone.

runbookBeats.title: Area 4 · Ruined barracks
read: Broken stone has swallowed much of the tower, but bedrolls and a narrow cleared path show that someone still sleeps here.
ask: Do you pass, search, disguise yourselves, or speak to the occupants?
run: Three goblins bunk here. A loud fight draws one goblin from area 7 to investigate; if that scout does not return or raises alarm, the others respond.
The eastern passage through rubble is safe despite its appearance.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal the southwest room when entered; place three goblins only when visible.
private: Adventure p. 37.

runbookBeats.title: Area 5 · Storeroom and Sildar’s gear
read: Spoiled provisions and old casks crowd the room. Among them lie a bloodied coat of mail, a crossbow, and a sword bearing a familiar crest.
ask: What do you search or take? Do you recognize the equipment?
run: The chain mail, heavy crossbow, and longsword belong to Sildar. Record whether the party returns them; his equipped combat card is appropriate only after he regains gear.
A small cask contains dwarven brandy. A second glass within one hour poisons the drinker for one hour, per the book.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal the storeroom; do not show the significance of its gear until the characters inspect it.
private: Adventure p. 37.

runbookBeats.title: Area 6 · Hobgoblin barracks
read: This room is surprisingly orderly. Weapons hang on brackets above four pallets, and the floor has been swept clear of rubble.
ask: Do you parley, withdraw, or fight? Who can see the door?
run: Four hobgoblins defend this room and respond quickly to the sentries’ alarm. They usually ignore noise elsewhere unless their own room is threatened.
Hobgoblin: AC 18, HP 11, speed 30, longsword +3 for 1d8+1; longbow +3 for 1d8+1. Once per turn, Martial Advantage adds 2d6 when an ally is within 5 feet of the target.
A light, carved quarterstaff on the wall is worth 10 gp. Other mounted arms are ordinary.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal this room at entry; deploy four hobgoblins if still present.
private: Adventure pp. 37–38; SRD 5.1 hobgoblin p. 322.

runbookBeats.title: Area 7 · Banquet hall
read: Once a grand hall, this chamber now smells of stale food and a neglected brazier. Goblin voices rise around two scarred tables.
ask: Do you enter openly, use the noise as cover, or try another route?
run: Seven ordinary goblins and Yegg, their 12-HP cook, are here initially. Reconcile any scout sent to area 4 before deploying this wave.
If Yegg falls, surviving goblins flee east or west, avoiding the trapped north route. They need not fight to the last.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal tables and benches; only place goblins that remain here after alarm movement.
private: Adventure p. 38. Yegg plus seven goblins is eight creatures total.

runbookBeats.title: Area 8 · Dark hall and grick
read: A narrow, lightless hall bears carvings that do not match its current occupants. Heavy curtains hang to the north, and a stone brazier stands between them.
ask: What light do you carry? Do you examine the carvings or move beneath the ledges?
run: A grick watches from an upper rocky ledge. Compare its Stealth to the party’s Perception to determine who notices it; do not give automatic surprise.

Grick: AC 14, HP 27, climb 30; tentacles +4 for 2d6+2 slashing. If they hit, it can make a beak +4 for 1d6+2 piercing against the same target. Its resistance to nonmagical weapon damage needs manual review in the damage panel.

DC 10 Intelligence (Religion) identifies the old human gods in the carvings. A gold sun-elf statuette worth 100 gp is hidden under coal in the brazier. It can answer one augury-like question for a non-evil creature, then loses that power.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal the hall first. Show the grick token or reveal art only after it drops from its hiding place.
private: Adventure pp. 38–39; SRD 5.1 grick p. 318. Do not reveal the hidden statuette before discovery.

runbookBeats.title: Area 9 · Goblin shrine
read: A stone altar lies beneath a blood-dark cloth. A goblin in ritual scraps fusses over gold-colored implements while two acolytes watch the curtains.
ask: Do you interrupt, negotiate, or pass without drawing attention?
run: Lhupo, a goblin with 12 HP, and two ordinary goblins occupy the shrine. If they heard the grick fight, they hide behind the altar and cannot be surprised.
The human-made chalice, knife, and censer are worth 150 gp, 60 gp, and 120 gp respectively if taken.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal the shrine beyond the curtains; place its occupants when they are seen.
private: Adventure p. 39. The objects are art treasure, not spellcasting tools.

runbookBeats.title: Area 10 · South postern gate
read: An overgrown path climbs toward an iron door protected by the wall above it. Narrow slits overlook the approach.
ask: Do you test the lock, watch the slits, or search for another entrance?
run: The door is locked: DC 15 Dexterity with thieves’ tools or DC 25 Strength to break it. The goblins in area 7 can be heard from the arrow slits if the party pauses.
The goblins do not actively watch this path, but loud noise draws their attention and can raise the alarm.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal only the gate and path from the direction of approach.
private: Adventure p. 39.

runbookBeats.title: Area 11 · Concealed north entrance
read: A fallen tower lies under dusty canvas and brush. A few old crates remain where a storeroom once stood.
ask: Where do you search? Does anyone inspect the outer wall?
run: From outside, DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) spots signs of a path to the concealed entrance. If actively searching the castle’s exterior for a hidden way in, DC 10 Wisdom (Perception) spots the canvas door.
This entrance can allow a quieter route toward the king’s side of the castle. Record whether the party leaves the canvas disturbed.
runbookBeats.tv: Do not show the concealed canvas entrance before the party finds it.
private: Adventure p. 39.

runbookBeats.title: Area 12 · Guard barracks
read: Four pallets line a cramped guardroom. A coal brazier glows, and a curtain conceals an arch to the north.
ask: Can the guards see you? Do you block the north route or let one run?
run: Two loyal hobgoblins guard this room. At the start of combat, one runs to warn Grol in area 14 and returns two rounds later if able.
Track that warning explicitly; it changes Vyerith’s position in the final room.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal the east barracks; place its two guards when seen.
private: Adventure p. 40.

runbookBeats.title: Area 13 · Owlbear tower
read: Something heavy shifts beyond the barred door. The wood shudders once, then a low animal breath fills the silence.
ask: Do you open the bar, leave it closed, or prepare a way out?
run: The owlbear has AC 13, HP 59, speed 40; one beak +7 for 1d10+5 and one claws +7 for 2d8+5 on its turn. It is dangerous for a level-2 party.
Fresh meat distracts it. If freed and not blocked, it flees the castle, attacking creatures that get in its way. Releasing it can earn the same printed XP as defeating it.
A chest on a high ledge requires DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) to notice; it holds 90 ep, 120 gp, a healing potion, silence scroll, and revivify scroll.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal the tower but hide the owlbear until the barred door opens and it is visible.
private: Adventure p. 40; SRD 5.1 owlbear pp. 339–340. The ledge chest is not visible from the floor.

runbookBeats.title: Area 14 · Gundren, Grol, and Vyerith
read: Voices cut through the door: a harsh demand, then a smooth reply. Inside, furs cover the floor. A battered dwarf lies still near a table while a towering bugbear argues with a dark-clad visitor.
ask: Do you listen longer, speak through the door, strike first, or try to protect Gundren?
run: King Grol is a 45-HP bugbear. Snarl is an 18-HP wolf. Vyerith is a 52-HP doppelganger disguised as a drow emissary of the Black Spider; its true nature is secret.

Grol wants payment for Gundren and his map. Vyerith wants the dwarf silenced and the map destroyed after questioning him. If warned, Vyerith may hide near the northeast exit. If Grol falls, Vyerith tries to kill Gundren and escape with the map toward area 11; if cornered, it fights.
Gundren is unconscious and stable at 0 HP. Grol can threaten him as a hostage. Allow rescue, bargaining, retreat, and pursuit rather than treating this only as a boss fight.
The map and treasure are in a sack under Grol’s mattress: 220 sp, 160 ep, three healing potions, and Gundren’s map. Gundren does not know where Grol hid it.
If Gundren survives, he asks for Phandalin and later Wave Echo Cave. Record his exact condition and whether the map was recovered; do not presume either outcome.
runbookBeats.tv: Reveal the room when the door opens. Show Gundren on the TV only once seen; keep Vyerith’s true form private until revealed.
private: Adventure pp. 40–41. The Redbrand delivery is custom campaign continuity; the Grol/Vyerith bargaining scene and treasure are printed.

runbookBeats.title: Optional consequence · Returning war band
read: Boots and low voices approach through the trees. A returning patrol has found the castle less quiet than it expected.
ask: Do you hide, negotiate, retreat, or stand your ground?
run: Optional printed complication: Targor Bloodsword, a hobgoblin with 20 HP, leads two ordinary hobgoblins and two wolves.
Targor has ambitions of succeeding Grol. A credible offer and DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) can convince him to let the party pass rather than avenge the king.
Use this only if it improves pacing and follows actual travel. A depleted party needs a visible escape route.
runbookBeats.tv: Show a woodland or castle approach map only if the returning patrol meets the party. Do not spawn it by default.
private: Adventure p. 41.

runbookBeats.title: Close · Record the trail to the mine
ask: What do you do with Gundren, the map, Sildar’s gear, prisoners, and any bargains?
Which route or promise matters next? What did each character actually learn?
run: Record Gundren alive, dead, missing, or still captive; whether the map is held by party, Vyerith, Grol’s survivors, or someone else; and each room left unresolved.
If rescued and escorted to Phandalin, Gundren’s printed offer is 25 gp each and a 10-percent share of a working mine. Treat it as his offer, not immediate cash or a guaranteed future.
Record XP or milestone only for accomplished events. Track healing potions, scrolls, Sildar’s gear, alarms, allies, and any Castle survivors.
Keep Trista’s BELOW token private unless she reveals it. Do not make the mine map explain the Echo mystery by itself.
choices: If the castle remains active, keep this session save for next play.
If the map is secured, the next pack is Wave Echo Cave after rest and player choice.
runbookBeats.tv: Return to the town map or a calm scene. Publish only facts the party witnessed.
private: Adventure p. 41. Session 3 outcomes must be entered after actual play, not prewritten as history.

spells.notes: Cantrip · action · minor magical effect within 10 ft.

spells.name: Ray of Frost
spells.notes: Cantrip · ranged spell attack +6 · 1d8 cold and speed −10 ft.

spells.name: Toll the Dead
spells.notes: Cantrip · Wisdom save DC 13 · 1d8 necrotic, or 1d12 if target is wounded.

spells.name: Spare the Dying
spells.notes: Cantrip · action · touch a creature at 0 HP to stabilize it.

spells.name: Guidance
spells.notes: Cantrip · touch · concentration up to 1 minute · +1d4 to one ability check.

spells.name: Command
spells.notes: Domain spell · Wisdom save DC 13 · one-word command within 60 ft.

spells.name: Identify
spells.notes: Domain spell · touch · learn magical properties; ritual possible; material pearl required.

spells.name: Detect Magic
spells.notes: Wizard · Sense magic within 30 ft. · concentration up to 10 minutes · ritual possible.

spells.name: Comprehend Languages
spells.notes: Wizard · Understand literal meaning of languages for 1 hour · ritual possible.

spells.name: Find Familiar
spells.notes: Wizard · Summon a familiar · 1-hour cast or ritual · material cost applies.

spells.name: Magic Missile
spells.notes: Wizard · Action · three darts within 120 ft. · each deals 1d4+1 force; no attack roll.

spells.name: Shield
spells.notes: Wizard · Reaction · +5 AC until next turn and blocks Magic Missile.

spells.name: Catapult
spells.notes: Wizard · Xanathar’s · action · Dexterity save DC 14 · fling a 1–5 lb. object; 3d8 bludgeoning.

spells.name: Disguise Self
spells.notes: Wizard · Action · alter your appearance for 1 hour; inspection may reveal illusion.

spells.name: Feather Fall
spells.notes: Wizard · Reaction · slow up to five falling creatures within 60 ft.

spells.name: Witch Bolt
spells.notes: Wizard · Action · ranged spell attack +6 · 1d12 lightning, concentration; action to sustain.

spells.name: Cure Wounds
spells.notes: Cleric · Action · touch · restore 1d8+3 HP.

spells.name: Healing Word
spells.notes: Cleric · Bonus action · 60 ft. · restore 1d4+3 HP.

spells.name: Shield of Faith
spells.notes: Cleric · Bonus action · +2 AC to one creature · concentration up to 10 minutes.

spells.name: Bane
spells.notes: Cleric · Action · up to three creatures make Charisma saves DC 13; failures subtract 1d4 from attacks and saves · concentration.

spells.name: Bless
spells.notes: Cleric · Action · up to three creatures add 1d4 to attacks and saves · concentration.

spells.name: Create or Destroy Water
spells.notes: Cleric · Action · create or destroy water in an open container or rain/fog in a small area.

spells.name: Detect Evil and Good
spells.notes: Cleric · Action · sense certain supernatural creatures or consecration within 30 ft. · concentration.

spells.name: Detect Magic
spells.notes: Cleric · Sense magic within 30 ft. · concentration up to 10 minutes · ritual possible.

spells.name: Detect Poison and Disease
spells.notes: Cleric · Action · sense poison, poisonous creatures, or disease within 30 ft. · concentration; ritual.

spells.name: Guiding Bolt
spells.notes: Cleric · Action · ranged spell attack +5 · 4d6 radiant; next attack against target gains advantage.

spells.name: Inflict Wounds
spells.notes: Cleric · Action · melee spell attack +5 · 3d10 necrotic.

spells.name: Protection from Evil and Good
spells.notes: Cleric · Action · touch · protect from listed creature types · concentration; material component consumed.

spells.name: Purify Food and Drink
spells.notes: Cleric · Action or ritual · purify nonmagical food and drink in a 5-ft. radius.

spells.name: Sanctuary
spells.notes: Cleric · Bonus action · protected creature within 30 ft.; attackers make Wisdom save DC 13.

spells.name: Ceremony
spells.notes: Cleric · Ritual · 1 hour · special rites; gold material component consumed.

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.text: Once per day after a short rest, recover one expended 1st-level slot.

features.name: Knowledge Domain
features.text: Command and Identify are always prepared as domain spells.

features.name: Blessings of Knowledge
features.text: Two additional languages and double proficiency on Arcana and History checks.

features.name: Wizard Spellcasting
features.text: INT spell attack +6; save DC 14. Prepare wizard spells separately from cleric spells.

features.name: Cleric Spellcasting
features.text: WIS spell attack +5; save DC 13. Prepare cleric spells separately from wizard spells.

features.name: Training
features.text: Light armor, medium armor, shields; dagger, dart, light crossbow, quarterstaff, sling.

snapshot.notes: Player export shows Wizard 1 / Cleric 1, 17 max HP, 1d6 + 1d8 hit dice, 3 shared first-level slots, Knowledge Domain. DM table rule permits all listed Wizard and Cleric spells as available despite normal preparation limits. Command and Identify are domain spells. Earlier character exception Mind Sliver is absent from this export and is therefore not shown as a current cantrip.
snapshot.publicNotes: All listed Wizard and Cleric spells are available by DM table rule; both classes share three 1st-level slots.

ally-sildar.name: Sildar Hallwinter
ally-sildar.sourceStatus: Adventure p. 10–11; captive lacks armor and weapons
ally-sildar.notes: Captive at 1 HP and stripped of armor and weapons. Set AC and attacks from actual gear before using him in combat.

old-owl-well.terrain: Ruined tower, working well, tent, and broken courtyard walls.
old-owl-well.objective: Resolve the contact with Hamun Kost and survive if negotiations fail.
old-owl-well.starting: Hamun is near the tent. Twelve zombies are hidden in the tower, not visible at first.

waves.name: Hamun Kost
waves.note: Deploy only if he becomes a combatant.

waves.name: Tower zombies
waves.note: Reveal only those that actually emerge. Undead Fortitude needs a save after a qualifying 0-HP hit.

old-owl-well.reinforcements: Kost can call the zombies off temporarily to talk.
old-owl-well.nonCombat: Parley and a favor are supported by the room key.
old-owl-well.morale: Kost values his work and safety.
old-owl-well.retreat: Hillside and approach paths remain open.
old-owl-well.negotiation: He may trade information for the Wyvern Tor or Agatha errand.

wyvern-tor.terrain: Ravine, cave, boulder cover, and one outside sentry.
wyvern-tor.objective: Resolve the orc threat without overlooking the cave defenders.
wyvern-tor.starting: One ordinary orc watches outside; six ordinary orcs, Brughor (30 HP), and Gog the ogre are inside.

waves.name: Outside sentry
waves.note: Place the sentry when spotted. If it warns the cave, mark the defenders alerted.

waves.name: Cave force
waves.note: Six ordinary orcs plus Brughor and Gog. Do not deploy until seen or emerging.

wyvern-tor.reinforcements: Only the listed cave force; no automatic extra orcs.
wyvern-tor.morale: After Brughor falls, surviving orcs flee.
wyvern-tor.negotiation: The group can attempt a demand or bargain before blades are drawn.

tt-blights-1.terrain: Ruined Thundertree cottage and overgrowth; rubble and brush can slow movement.
tt-blights-1.objective: Explore, avoid, or survive the hidden plants.

waves.name: Hidden twig blights
waves.note: Compare Stealth and Perception before revealing.

tt-blights-1.reinforcements: Only nearby groups that hear the actual fight.
tt-blights-1.nonCombat: Scout, pass around the growth, or retreat.

tt-blights-2.terrain: Ruined Thundertree cottage and overgrowth; rubble and brush can slow movement.
tt-blights-2.objective: Explore, avoid, or survive the hidden plants.

waves.name: Hidden twig blights
waves.note: Area-1 survivors can move here; do not duplicate.

tt-blights-2.reinforcements: Surviving area-1 blights can join after one round. Move their existing tokens.
tt-blights-2.nonCombat: Scout, pass around the growth, or retreat.

tt-zombies-3.terrain: Brown Horse tavern; walls and bar provide cover.
tt-zombies-3.starting: Four ash zombies slumped and prone until living creatures enter.

waves.name: Tavern zombies
waves.note: Track Ash Puff on each zombie’s first damage.

tt-blights-5.terrain: Ruined Thundertree cottage and overgrowth; rubble and brush can slow movement.
tt-blights-5.objective: Explore, avoid, or survive the hidden plants.

waves.name: Hidden twig blights
waves.note: If disturbed, reveal arrivals in pairs at each door over three rounds.

tt-blights-5.reinforcements: Only nearby groups that hear the actual fight.
tt-blights-5.nonCombat: Scout, pass around the growth, or retreat.

tt-spiders-6.terrain: Web-filled lane and ruined store; web squares are difficult terrain.
tt-spiders-6.starting: Two giant spiders hidden on inner walls.

waves.name: Store spiders
waves.note: Reveal when seen or when they attack.

tt-spiders-6.nonCombat: Go around; cut webs; escape restrained creatures.

tt-dragon-7.terrain: Tower, attached cottage, rooftop opening, 40-foot ceiling.
tt-dragon-7.objective: Survive, negotiate, or drive away Venomfang; killing it is not required.
tt-dragon-7.starting: Young green dragon concealed in the tower until discovered.

waves.name: Venomfang
waves.note: Do not surprise players with a routine combat: show warning signs and room to retreat.

tt-dragon-7.reinforcements: Cultists may approach only if their actions bring them here.
tt-dragon-7.nonCombat: Parley, leave, scout, or return at higher level.
tt-dragon-7.morale: At half HP it flies away.
tt-dragon-7.retreat: Open tower roof and village paths.

tt-zombies-8.terrain: Old smithy with rotten timber and anvils.
tt-zombies-8.objective: Pass or defeat two ash zombies.
tt-zombies-8.starting: Two ash zombies prone until disturbed.

waves.name: Smithy zombies
waves.note: Track each Ash Puff separately.

tt-zombies-8.morale: Pursue once they see the party.

tt-zombies-11.terrain: Intact garrison, bunks, narrow windows, rooftop ladder.
tt-zombies-11.objective: Pass or defeat five ash zombies.

waves.name: Garrison zombies
waves.note: Old armor does not improve AC.

tt-blights-12.terrain: Ruined Thundertree cottage and overgrowth; rubble and brush can slow movement.
tt-blights-12.objective: Explore, avoid, or survive the hidden plants.

waves.name: Hidden twig blights
waves.note: Loud combat can draw area-13 cultists to investigate.

tt-blights-12.reinforcements: Only nearby groups that hear the actual fight.
tt-blights-12.nonCombat: Scout, pass around the growth, or retreat.

tt-cultists-13.terrain: Barred cottage with shutters and several interior rooms.
tt-cultists-13.objective: Learn their intent and choose whether to bargain.
tt-cultists-13.starting: Six cultists including Favric, hidden inside.

waves.name: Favric and cultists
waves.note: Talk first; four stand guard, two rest.

tt-cultists-13.reinforcements: No automatic dragon support. Favric may seek an alliance.
tt-cultists-13.nonCombat: Talk, watch, withdraw, or expose Favric’s plan.
tt-cultists-13.morale: Followers flee if Favric is captured or killed.
tt-cultists-13.negotiation: Favric claims he can broker a dragon alliance.

castle-archers.terrain: Two arrow-slit posts at the broken gate; defenders have three-quarters cover through the slits.
castle-archers.objective: Enter without giving the entire castle warning.
castle-archers.starting: Two goblins in each post, four total, hidden until noticed or firing.

waves.name: Two archer posts
waves.note: Place two in each area-3 post; do not place all in one room.

castle-archers.reinforcements: If the sentries shout, area 4 goblins and area 6 hobgoblins can rush to the trapped hall.
castle-archers.nonCombat: Stealth, Redbrand disguise, or another entrance can bypass the posts.
castle-archers.retreat: The ruined gate and forest remain open.
castle-archers.negotiation: Bluffing as Glasstaff envoys is supported by the book.

castle-trap.terrain: Area 2 hall with hidden tripwire, loose ceiling, and rubble.
castle-trap.objective: Detect or avoid a falling-rubble trap.
castle-trap.nonCombat: Passive Perception 20 or active DC 10 Perception while searching; DC 10 Dexterity save, 3d6 bludgeoning or half.

castle-barracks.terrain: Southwest ruined barracks and safe rubble passage.
castle-barracks.starting: Three goblins remain unless they responded to an alarm elsewhere.

waves.name: Barracks goblins
waves.note: Reconcile earlier alarms before deploying.

castle-barracks.reinforcements: Loud noise attracts one banquet goblin scout.
castle-barracks.negotiation: A captured goblin may know castle layout.

castle-hobgoblins.starting: Four hobgoblins; they respond to sentries but usually ignore distant noise.

waves.name: Hobgoblin barracks
waves.note: Remember Martial Advantage if an ally is adjacent to a target.

castle-hobgoblins.reinforcements: Sentry alarm can draw them into area 2.
castle-hobgoblins.nonCombat: A convincing Redbrand envoy story may open conversation.
castle-hobgoblins.morale: They defend their room and allies.
castle-hobgoblins.negotiation: They can assess a claim to work for the Black Spider.

castle-banquet.terrain: Tables, benches, and a large hall with several exits.
castle-banquet.objective: Pass or resolve the goblin mess hall.
castle-banquet.starting: Yegg (12 HP) and seven ordinary goblins, minus any scout who left.

waves.name: Banquet hall
waves.note: Eight total before scouts move. Place only those still here.

castle-banquet.reinforcements: One goblin may already be scouting area 4. Trap noise alerts this room.
castle-banquet.nonCombat: Bluff, avoid, or use the many exits.
castle-banquet.morale: When Yegg falls, survivors flee east or west and avoid the trapped north hall.
castle-banquet.negotiation: Food, rank, and Grol’s authority can be used in a bluff.

castle-grick.terrain: Dark hall, high ledges, curtains, and brazier.
castle-grick.objective: Cross the hall or confront the hidden grick.
castle-grick.starting: One grick concealed on a rocky ledge.

waves.name: Grick revealed
waves.note: Deploy when noticed or when it attacks.

castle-grick.reinforcements: Combat here prevents the area-9 goblins from being surprised.
castle-grick.nonCombat: Move cautiously, use light, avoid the ledges, or withdraw.
castle-grick.morale: Predatory creature; it can be avoided.

castle-shrine.terrain: Altar and heavy curtains; room can provide cover.
castle-shrine.objective: Deal with Lhupo and two acolytes.
castle-shrine.starting: Lhupo (12 HP) plus two goblins, prepared if grick fight was heard.

waves.name: Shrine occupants
waves.note: Do not give them surprise if alerted by area 8.

castle-shrine.reinforcements: Noise may carry into nearby halls.
castle-shrine.negotiation: Religious claims or a Redbrand disguise can be tested.

castle-guards.terrain: East guardroom with curtain leading toward area 14.
castle-guards.objective: Prevent or account for warning to Grol.
castle-guards.starting: Two hobgoblins; one runs to warn Grol at combat start.

waves.name: King’s guards
waves.note: One leaves to warn area 14 and returns two rounds later if able.

castle-guards.reinforcements: Grol and Vyerith react to a successful warning; do not auto-deploy them in this room.
castle-guards.nonCombat: Block the route, deceive, or retreat.
castle-guards.negotiation: They may test a claim of business with the king.

castle-owlbear.terrain: Dark tower, barred door, and high ledge.
castle-owlbear.objective: Survive, distract, or free a captive owlbear.
castle-owlbear.starting: One owlbear remains behind the barred door.

waves.name: Owlbear
waves.note: Deploy only when the door opens and the creature is visible.

castle-owlbear.reinforcements: If released, its movement can disrupt nearby rooms rather than creating a fresh monster.
castle-owlbear.nonCombat: Fresh meat distracts it; a clear exit lets it flee.
castle-owlbear.morale: It seeks freedom and food, not loyalty to goblins.
castle-owlbear.negotiation: Animal handling and food may buy time; it does not speak.

castle-king.terrain: Grol’s quarters, table, furs, and concealed northeast escape. Gundren was left at an inn after actual play.
castle-king.objective: Resolve Grol and Vyerith’s conflict; recover only possessions actually established at the castle.
castle-king.starting: Grol 45 HP, Snarl 18 HP, Vyerith 52 HP disguised as a drow. Do not place Gundren here or assume Glasstaff has joined this room.

waves.name: King’s quarters
waves.note: Keep Vyerith’s true type private. If warned, position it near the northeast escape.

castle-king.reinforcements: A guard from area 12 may return two rounds after warning Grol.
castle-king.nonCombat: Bargaining, rescue, stealth, or retreat can alter the fight.
castle-king.morale: If Grol dies, Vyerith may flee through area 11 with anything it actually possesses; cornered, it fights.
castle-king.retreat: Northeast concealed route and entry door.
castle-king.negotiation: Grol and Vyerith may bargain over information or possessions they actually hold. Gundren is not their hostage.

castle-warband.terrain: Forest or trail outside the castle; optional returning patrol.
castle-warband.objective: Avoid, bargain with, or defeat Targor’s group.
castle-warband.starting: Targor 20 HP, two ordinary hobgoblins, and two wolves.

waves.name: Returning patrol
waves.note: Optional; do not deploy automatically on exit.

castle-warband.nonCombat: DC 15 Persuasion may persuade Targor that he should succeed Grol.
castle-warband.morale: Targor is ambitious rather than suicidal.
castle-warband.negotiation: Offer him a path to leadership or pass quietly.

points.title: Barthen’s Provisions
points.clue: A busy supply shop stands beside the road into town.
points.note: The party begins Session 2 here. Delivery and payment only happen if played.

points.title: Stonehill Inn
points.clue: Warm light and voices come from the largest inn near the green.
points.note: Rumors and Sildar’s lodging; Lost Mine pp. 15–16.

points.title: Townmaster’s Hall
points.clue: A modest public hall sits on the south side of the green.
points.note: Harbin Wester; town notices and orc reward.

points.title: Lionshield Coster
points.clue: A sturdy trading post displays a blue lion shield.
points.note: Linene Graywind; stolen goods from Cragmaw Hideout.

points.title: Miner’s Exchange
points.clue: Prospectors come and go with pouches of ore and dust.
points.note: Halia Thornton; do not announce her private goals.

points.title: Shrine of Luck
points.clue: A small shrine stands near the road and the town green.
points.note: Sister Garaele; Agatha lead if offered.

points.title: Sleeping Giant
points.clue: The tap house has a rougher crowd than the inn.
points.note: Redbrand pressure can arise here; do not place foes until the scene warrants it.

points.title: Alderleaf Farm
points.clue: Fields and a farmhouse lie along the edge of town.
points.note: Qelline and Carp; allow clues to emerge through play.

points.title: Edermath Orchard
points.clue: Rows of fruit trees lead to a cottage on the west side.
points.note: Daran Edermath; Old Owl Well lead.

points.title: Tresendar Manor ruins
points.clue: A ruined manor overlooks the settlement from a low hill.
points.note: The visible ruins are public. The Redbrand entrance and tunnel remain private.

points.title: Hillside tunnel
points.clue: A narrow opening cuts into the slope below the manor.
points.note: Reveal only after the party finds this entrance.

points.title: Ruined village green
points.clue: Grass and saplings have overtaken the old center of Conyberry.
points.note: Custom orientation landmark; the published settlement is abandoned.

points.title: Westward ruins
points.clue: Only foundations remain among the trees.
points.note: Custom orientation landmark. Do not imply a keyed encounter.

points.title: Broken stone building
points.clue: A roofless stone building faces the old road.
points.note: Custom orientation landmark. Let players describe their search.

points.title: Old riverside building
points.clue: A large ruin stands near the watercourse.
points.note: Custom orientation landmark, not a published room key.

points.title: Forest trail
points.clue: A narrow path disappears into the western woods.
points.note: Reveal when the party follows the Agatha lead or discovers the path.

points.title: Western cottages
points.clue: Broken cottages stand among ash-dusted trees.
points.note: Areas 1–2. Keep occupants and hazards private.

points.title: Old inn
points.clue: A weathered sign hangs above the remains of an inn.
points.note: Area 3, Brown Horse. Reveal only what is visible.

points.title: Boarded cottage
points.clue: This cottage is in better repair than the surrounding ruins.
points.note: Area 4, Druid’s Watch. Reidoth is not on the public marker.

points.title: Ruined store
points.clue: Webs and broken beams cover a former shop.
points.note: Area 6. Do not reveal spiders before seen.

points.title: Old tower
points.clue: A round tower rises above the overgrown settlement.
points.note: Area 7. Do not reveal Venomfang before seen.

points.title: Old smithy
points.clue: A ruined forge sits beside the eastern track.
points.note: Area 8.

points.title: Herbalist’s shop
points.clue: A small shop is almost swallowed by vines.
points.note: Area 9.

points.title: Town square
points.clue: A worn statue stands at the meeting of the old paths.
points.note: Area 10.

points.title: Old garrison
points.clue: Heavy stone walls still outline a guard post.
points.note: Area 11.

points.title: Eastern cottage
points.clue: A cottage stands at the far edge of the ruins.
points.note: Area 13. Do not identify the cultists until discovered.

points.title: The Yawning Portal
points.clue: The famous inn is a gathering place for adventurers in Castle Ward.
points.note: Campaign home base. The well descends to Undermountain.

points.title: Castle Waterdeep
points.clue: The city’s fortress dominates the high ground above the harbor.
points.note: Public landmark; city map is a schematic, not a street-accurate plan.

points.title: Deepwater Harbor
points.clue: Ships crowd the quays beside the Dock Ward.
points.note: Public landmark.

points.title: City of the Dead
points.clue: Gardens and memorials fill the walled cemetery.
points.note: Public landmark.

points.title: North Gate
points.clue: The northern road enters the city through its great wall.
points.note: Public landmark.

points.title: Second Margin bookshop
points.clue: A bookshop awaits investigation in Castle Ward.
points.note: Custom Echo Below location. Reveal only after the party learns of it.

points.title: Lantern House
points.clue: A familiar refuge lies among the streets of the Southern Ward.
points.note: Custom hub location. Reveal when introduced.

points.title: Neverwinter
points.clue: A great city on the Sword Coast, where Gundren hired the party for the journey south.
points.note: Starting point. This map is an approximate campaign overview, not a measured travel map.

points.title: Thundertree
points.clue: Ruins lie at the edge of Neverwinter Wood.
points.note: Chapter 3 optional branch. Reidoth can help locate Cragmaw Castle. Do not reveal the dragon or cultists on the map.

points.title: Agatha’s lair
points.clue: An old path leaves the ruined village and winds into the woods.
points.note: Sister Garaele’s optional lead. Reveal the exact destination only when the party learns it.

points.title: Conyberry
points.clue: The eastern trail reaches an abandoned village.
points.note: Chapter 3 optional branch; Agatha’s trail begins nearby.

points.title: Cragmaw Castle
points.clue: An old stronghold stands somewhere within the forest.
points.note: DM continuity: Redbrands abducted Gundren and delivered him here. The party has not learned this. Reveal only after a credible lead.

points.title: Old Owl Well
points.clue: Ancient stones rise from the eastern hills.
points.note: Daran Edermath’s optional lead. Hamun Kost and the undead remain secret.

points.title: Wyvern Tor
points.clue: A rocky hill overlooks the southern wilds.
points.note: Optional orc threat from the Townmaster’s Hall notice. Do not reveal occupants until discovered.

points.title: Triboar Trail ambush
points.clue: Here the party found Gundren’s horses and fought goblins on the road.
points.note: Session 1 opening. The party followed the goblin trail to Cragmaw Hideout.

points.title: Cragmaw Hideout
points.clue: The party followed a goblin trail to this cave and rescued Sildar.
points.note: Session 1 complete: Klarg dead, Yeemik left in charge. Gundren’s destination was not learned.

points.title: Phandalin
points.clue: A frontier mining town at the end of the supply road. The party has reached Barthen’s Provisions.
points.note: Current campaign hub. Open the Phandalin town map for shops, NPCs, and local leads.

points.title: Tresendar Manor ruins
points.clue: A ruined manor watches over Phandalin from a low hill.
points.note: The ruins are visible from town. Redbrand hideout entrances and occupants stay private until discovered.

points.title: Wave Echo Cave
points.clue: A hidden cave lies somewhere in the Sword Mountains.
points.note: Do not reveal the point or location until Gundren’s map, testimony, or another credible discovery gives the party its position. Chapter 4.

DM notes: 2 · Triboar Trail and Neverwinter Wood
DM notes: 1 · Choose the lead, not the destination
